001.summary: The first game ever played with the deck (no result logged; a pod of three at home). A Sol Ring opening made it fast, and Brallin and Shabraz got big off discards and draws. A late wheel (the note's 'Edge of Eons', which on this list reads as Echo of Eons) 'almost killed Stuart through commander damage'. After that it went grindy: Brallin was removed twice and picked up commander tax, the deck drew no ramp past the opening, and it had no creature or enchantment removal against Steven's counters. Played on v7 (decklist_sha256 ce0ceaa6…, 2026-10-06), not the current v2.2.0. Several cards the note names have since left the 99: Mana Geyser (gone by v1.3.0), Swiftfoot Boots, Echo of Eons and the 'wheel on a stick' (Magus of the Wheel on that list) were cut at v2.0.0, and the note's 'Jessica's Will' was cut at v2.1.0 (answers-v1). Read those as notes about the list that was played, not errors.

opponents.evidence: Steven had a bunch of freaking counters that he was playing

cards.why: 'it started off pretty fast, but that's because I had Sol Ring in my opening hand'
'Lightning Greaves ... were really good and and protected them' (the note says the same of the Swiftfoot Boots then in the list)
'Brawn got taken out a couple times' and 'he got removed a couple times and then the tax came on'
a wheel 'made Shabraz really big' and 'almost killed Stuart through commander damage'
'I never pulled Jessica's Will or Mana Geyser' while the deck felt 'a little light on the ramp'. It has since left the 99

decisions.spot: which commander to deploy first, and whether to hold the second (and the wheels) until hand and board suit the pair: 'bring one out ... get that thing big and then like bring the second one out later and then start doing the wheels'
firing a wheel that discards 'some really useful things because I just needed to do the wheel'

takeaways: The two commanders cost nine mana as a pair ('basically equivalent to the Ur-Dragon'), and one removal stacks tax on top. Ramp past the opening hand felt light.
Protection (Lightning Greaves and the Boots then in the list) worked, but Brallin was still removed twice.
The deck had no creature or enchantment removal when the board needed pruning, and too little interaction against a counterspell seat, so the late game went grindy.
Piloting plan: one commander first, grow it, add the second later, and fire the wheels when both are on the board with protection up.
The pilot wants wheels that do a second job (a counter plus a wheel, removal plus a wheel) so that each slot covers two needs.
Wheels split the table ('people either loved it or hated it'), and they can cost the pilot his own good cards.

open_questions.question: On the current list, how often are both commanders (four plus five mana) on the battlefield by turns six to eight, and how often with one tax added after a removal?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the pilot reads the pair as a nine-drop and felt ramp-light. Every wheel's payoff assumes both commanders are out

open_questions.question: Does the deck carry enough creature and enchantment removal, plus interaction against counterspells, to prune a board and get a wheel through a counterspell seat?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the note blames the grindy late game on 'I didn't have enough interaction or removal'

open_questions.question: Which wheel effects in the corpus also counter a spell or remove permanents, the 'align on both axes' cards the pilot asked for?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the pilot named this as what 'would be money', and he asked for the research agent to queue explorations

open_questions.question: Is 'one commander first, the second later, wheels only with both out' the right piloting plan for this pair?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the note proposes it as 'a piloting strategy', and game 002 says the same about when wheels should land

002.summary: A loss in a four-player pod at Oliver's, played on v8 (decklist_sha256 fda57c5a…, the v1.3.0 list), not the current v2.0.0. The pilot mulliganed and doubted the hand he kept, which had one playable creature and a bunch of wheels. Shabraz's wheels 'went pretty well', but his main finding is that the deck runs too many wheels. Wheels should be few, held as finishers for when both commanders are already out, partly because making the table discard over and over is politically costly. The v2.0.0 voltron merge has since cut several wheels from that list (Echo of Eons, Magus of the Wheel and Time Reversal among them). This annotation records what the pilot said; it does not judge whether that merge settles his point.

opponents.evidence: Oliver is making people discard creatures on the board and all this other stuff

decisions.spot: keep or mulligan a hand with 'only one playable creature in it and a bunch of wheels'
when to fire a wheel: early as card flow, or held until 'Shabraz and Brallin are already out, they're kind of big' as a finisher

takeaways: Too many wheels: 'I think there's too many wheels', and the kept hand had one creature and several wheels.
Wheels are finishers. They should land when both commanders are on the table and already big, then chain into a second wheel, with red open for trample.
Repeated wheels cost goodwill at the table ('Making people discard their hand is not something people enjoy'), which is one more reason to make them 'few and far between'.
Discount goldfish figures on this deck: they leave out removal and opponent interaction, and that 'just moves the deck in the wrong direction'.

open_questions.question: On the v2.0.0 list, how often does an opening seven hold at most one creature alongside two or more wheels, and how did that rate move from v1.3.0?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the pilot's 'too many wheels' finding came from exactly that keep. A paired before-and-after rate would show whether the voltron merge addressed it

open_questions.question: With both commanders out and grown, does a wheel followed by a second wheel, then a flying, trampling commander attack ('into another one ... flying trample big commander shark coming at you'), kill a seat through commander damage?
open_questions.why_it_matters: this is the finisher sequence the pilot wants wheels saved for. Only the single-Windfall base line is proved (stack 001), and stack 005 shows one Windfall is not a kill from 40

open_questions.question: Is the deck's wheel count right for a list where wheels are finishers rather than card flow?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the pilot proposed recalibrating the deck around that role, and game 001 also asked for wheels held until both commanders are out

003.summary: A short note after a game on v2.0.0 (decklist_sha256 c9186bd9…, the modal-voltron list of 2026-10-24), not the current v2.2.0; no result or table recorded, and the pilot logged the cause as raced (2026-10-28). The deck felt slow: 'no removal, slow to get cards out, got mana starved one round'. The pilot left open whether that was 'a sequencing thing' or 'the cards I saw'. answers-v1 (v2.1.0, 2026-10-26) added interaction after this game, so the 'no removal' read is about the list that was played.
takeaways: The deck read as slow ('it's slooooowwwww'), and the pilot could not tell sequencing from the draw: 'maybe it's a sequencing thing, maybe it's the cards I saw'.
'No removal' again, the same complaint as game 001, on the list before answers-v1 added interaction.
'Got mana starved one round', a second note after 001 ('a little light on the ramp') that the mana ran short.

open_questions.question: Did answers-v1 (v2.1.0) give the current list enough removal to answer the 'no removal' complaint of games 001 and 003, counting creature and enchantment answers in the 99?
open_questions.why_it_matters: two of the four logged games name missing removal, both on lists from before that merge; game 004, on the current list, does not

004.summary: A loss at Ryan's house on the list of the day (v2.2.0, decklist_sha256 8df06ee1…; the deck is now v3.0.0, and the note's 'Ledger card' and 'Bonnie/Annie' are no longer in the 99), cause raced. The draw/discard engine 'ran well and the sequencing felt right', but Sean kept a land-heavy opener with one wheel and few payoffs, held both commanders back to dodge a wipe while waiting for a wheel that never came, and Alex's warp deck, 'a faster class of deck', outpaced him. Since settled by the queue: Q012 found the land-and-ramp keep was good, Q013 led to the rule to cast the first commander on curve, and Q014 named Alex's turn-ending artifact and the answers to it (see data/opponents/tannuk-warp/NOTES.md).

opponents.evidence: Ramps to about 15 mana and warps out a large number of creatures.
Ryan on Slivers (nothing much popped off for Ryan)

cards.why: 'produced steady Treasure. That was the ramp the hand needed, and it may have been under-used'
in the opener, but Sean 'went first, so he never got the luck-counter version for any-color mana'
'Deflecting Swat was in hand this game too'; the note records it without saying it was cast

decisions.spot: keep or mulligan an opener of 'a lot of lands, ramp, one artifact dork and one wheel, but few creatures or payoffs'; Q012 has since read it as a good keep
hold both commanders 'to avoid a wipe and wait for a wheel', or cast the first on curve; Q013 has since settled on casting on curve
how hard to lean on Smothering Tithe's Treasure, which 'may have been under-used'

takeaways: The draw/discard loops carried the game: 'the Ledger card (connive: draw, discard) and Bonnie/Annie (haste, draw a card, discard a card)' moved Sean through the deck, he 'cast a lot of spells', and Alex said 'things were happening'. Neither piece is in the current 99 (v3.0.0), so the note names them as it wrote them.
Holding the commanders for a wheel cost tempo when no wheel came. The play rule adopted since (Q012, Q013): keep the land-and-ramp hand and cast the first commander on curve.
Alex's warp turns outpace Sharknado: 'without Alex's warp turns, Sharknado does much more'. The answers and their timing were worked out since (Q014).
Discard-a-card effects slow the deck, and the pilot wants the wheel count looked at.

open_questions.question: Is the wheel count on v2.2.0 right, and how much do the deck's discard-a-card costs ('Discard-a-card effects also slow the deck') drag on hand size and tempo?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the note's lesson asks to 'Look at wheel count and the discard-a-card drag'; Q012 to Q014 did not cover it, and game 002 called the wheels too many on an earlier list

005.summary: A late three-player loss at Sean's house on v2.2.0 (decklist_sha256 8df06ee1…, the same list as 004; the deck is now v3.0.0 and Marauding Mako and Lightning Greaves are not in the current 99). Alex, on Sean's Goblin Storm deck (the note's 'Zeta deck'), won: 'Purphoros was on the board pinging everybody for damage'. Sean again kept 'quite a bit of ramp' with small creatures and a wheel, grew Marauding Mako by +6/+6 off a wheel, but the commanders never came out and the sequencing 'felt a little off'. The pilot reads it as mostly piloting: 'I get distracted with like the little smaller creatures' instead of putting resources into the commander line.

opponents.evidence: Purphoros was on the board pinging everybody for damage
David was playing his new golem deck

cards.why: 'I did a wheel with Marauding Mako out there and I was able to discard like seven or six cards and give him plus six plus six'
'I did have things like Lightning Greaves and Ember Cleave, and like I just couldn't ever get the commander out with those things'

decisions.spot: a ramp-heavy opener with small creatures and a wheel: keep or mulligan ('I don't feel like I, I kept the right hand'), the same shape as 004's keep
with two or three cards in hand, whether to pay a discard-for-a-counter cost that draws nothing back, or hold the cards
spend the turn on the small discard creatures or on getting the first commander out and wheeling into it

takeaways: Put resources into the commander line first: 'get a one of those commanders out and start wheeling into it and make it big', rather than the small discard creatures.
Wheels are payoffs, not cards to hold: the wheel with Marauding Mako out discarded six or seven cards for +6/+6.
Discard costs without a draw attached strand a small hand: 'I'm sitting with like two or three cards in my hand ... I also don't want to discard any of these cards.'
The commanders are expensive and 'just aren't coming out fast enough'; the pilot likens it to the Ur-Dragon, which needed ramp to cast its commander sooner.
Sharknado 'still feels it has a good rating'; the pilot puts the loss on 'some piloting stuff and, and maybe some tuning'.

open_questions.question: On v3.0.0, by what turn is the first commander on the battlefield, and does a ramp-heavy keep with no payoff still reach it sooner, as Q012 found on v2.2.0?
open_questions.why_it_matters: two logged games (004, 005) on the same list end with the pilot questioning a ramp-heavy keep and saying the commanders came out too slowly; Q012's answer was read on a list that has since changed

open_questions.question: Which cards in the current 99 ask for a discard without drawing a card back, and how much do they cost a small hand against the deck's draw sources?
open_questions.why_it_matters: 004's lesson and 005 both name the discard-a-card drag ('I need that card draw'); 004's open question on it has not been answered

006.summary: Game 2 of a five-player night at Oliver's (Heliod won game 1; that game is not this deck's). Sharknado lost to Ryan's T'Vol going infinite around turn 8-9 with its lethal 'fully assembled except for the one card type that triggers it': Shabraz, Brallin, Fiery Emancipation, Smothering Tithe with 36 Treasure, Mystic Remora and Teferi's Ageless Insight on board and a tutor in hand aimed at Shark Typhoon, but no wheel was ever drawn. Played on v2.2.0 (decklist_sha256 8df06ee1...), not the current v3.0.0: Mystic Remora (gone by v2.3.0) and Embercleave (gone by v3.0.0) have since left the 99, so read those as notes about the list that was played.

opponents.evidence: Ryan went infinite with T'Vol around turn 8–9 before it came around again

cards.why: 'On board; 36 Treasure banked' — the mana for the planned Shark Typhoon cycle
'On board, drawing 2 per trigger'; with Teferi's Ageless Insight it dug 9-10 cards. Since left the 99
on board and part of the dig: 'Dug 9–10 cards off Remora and Teferi looking for any wheel'
'Wheel (Windfall or similar) — Never drawn'; after the game 'the first wheel ... was deep'
'keeps appearing early and getting discarded to the loot engine'. Since left the 99

decisions.spot: multipliers and 36 Treasure on board, a tutor in hand, no wheel: tutor Shark Typhoon now for the cycled flyer, or keep digging for a wheel (the pilot dug 9-10 cards, ideally for an instant-speed wheel on another player's turn)

takeaways: Payoffs lag the engine: Tithe, Remora and the Treasure came online reliably, the wheel did not. The note calls this the second straight log with the same finding.
The forced-discard half of the draw engine is sometimes a cost, not a benefit; the pilot would prefer modal draw where discarding is optional.
Defensive piloting held up: the deck survived several wraths and wipes.
The pilot holds every hypothesis from this game until two or three more games are logged; no swap off one game, and buying the proxied third of the list waits on the research.

open_questions.question: Was the planned line (tutored Shark Typhoon cycled off 36 Treasure for a ~34-power flyer, trample from Brallin, damage tripled by Fiery Emancipation) lethal on its own, or did it need the wheel the note says was missing?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the note says the board was lethal 'except for the one card type that triggers it' while also describing a Typhoon line that a tutor could reach; stack 012 proves the cycling payment, not the whole kill

open_questions.question: On the current list, how many wheels are there and on what turn does the first one typically arrive, against when Shabraz and the draw engines land?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the pilot's own first research request; 'payoffs lag the engine' is in two logs running

open_questions.question: Which tutors in the list can find a wheel, and what should each tutor fetch when the board has multipliers but no wheel?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the pilot asked for a 'what to tutor for when' map; this game turned on that choice

open_questions.question: Are there more multipliers and equipment than wheels to feed them, and does draw with optional discard fit the hand better than forced loots?
open_questions.why_it_matters: two of the pilot's research requests; the list has changed twice since (v2.3.0, v3.0.0), so check against v3.0.0

007.summary: First game on the newly sleeved v2.3.0 (decklist_sha256 36d865a6...; no result or opponents logged). The pilot found the wheels, got the commanders big and 'actually could have won', but the deck felt 'clunky and slow as hell', brittle because the two commanders cost 9 mana with two taxes, and the draw-and-discard felt 'laborious' and 'a bit convoluted'. The list has since become the Shabraz-first v3.0.0.
takeaways: The deck worked mechanically (wheels found, commanders big, a win was available) and still was not fun: 'clunky and slow', 'convoluted'.
Two commanders mean two taxes and 9 mana to deploy both; the pilot reads that as brittleness.
The card draw and discard is 'laborious'; the stack triggers themselves are 'fine'. Same shape as 006's note that forced discard is sometimes a cost.

open_questions.question: Does the Shabraz-first v3.0.0 address what made v2.3.0 feel slow and laborious, the 9-mana commander pair and the forced-discard loot steps?
open_questions.why_it_matters: 'slow' recurs across 003, 006 and 007; 008 on v3.0.0 was lost to a misplay, so it does not yet answer this

008.summary: Game 3 of an 0-3 night at Oliver's against an optimized bracket 3 table that aims to win around turn four. Oliver landed Krenko; with the table asking for the kill, Sean held Swords to Plowshares and a second two-mana removal spell, cast Shabraz instead, then passed another turn with open mana, and Oliver went off for 30-plus damage in one turn. Played on the current v3.0.0. The pilot calls it '100% piloting error' and wants no deck changes.

opponents.evidence: Oliver went off; Sean took 30-plus damage in one turn

decisions.spot: Oliver's Krenko just landed, the table names it, Sean holds Swords to Plowshares and a second two-mana removal spell: remove Krenko, or cast Shabraz for momentum (and the turn after, with Shabraz out and mana open, remove it then)

takeaways: When the whole table names the threat and only you can answer it, answer it. Threat removal beats tempo.
Kill on sight at this pod: Purphoros (Tom), Krenko (Oliver).
Deny the Sol Ring opener: early artifact removal is a legitimate tempo play against this pod.
Oliver's and Tom's bracket 3 decks are optimized with a turn-four clock; the B-team's bracket 3 runs a turn 6-7 clock.
No deck changes: track Shabraz across more games before any tuning review.

open_questions.question: How many answers can v3.0.0 aim at a commander like Krenko on the turn it lands, and is enchantment removal adequately covered?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the pilot asks for a standing enchantment-removal slot audit across decks; the deck must be able to answer when the table names the threat

open_questions.question: How often is Shabraz on the battlefield by turn four, against a table whose clock is about turn four?
open_questions.why_it_matters: this table's clock is about turn four, and the engine model puts Shabraz's first window at turn four or five
